To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the active shear area, which is the average of the gross shear area and the net shear area, should be used in the block shear equation.
the shear stresses are zero at the free end of the connection, and that the active shear plane is midway between the gross shear plane and the net shear plane.
the block shear failure of a bolted steel connection occurs along the active shear area, which is located midway between the gross shear area and the net shear area of the connection block.
In summary, our research is concerned with

developing a better understanding of the shear failure mechanism of block shear connections, which will be of value for the future revision of the design equations for block shear connections in the steel codes.
the development of an improved design equation for the block shear capacity, and this paper presents the finite-element results that confirm the veracity of the improved design equation.
the development of a rational design equation that will consistently predict the governing failure mode in the block shear failure of bolted connections.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the active shear plane concept should be incorporated in the design codes.
the block shear capacity can be calculated by using the active shear area, which is midway between the gross area and the net area.
the block shear equations in the design codes worldwide should be revised to adopt the active shear area.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the shear failure planes of block shear connections do not coincide with the gross or the shear planes, but lie between the gross and net shear areas.
the active shear area should be used for calculating the block-shear capacity.
the active shear area should be used in the block shear design equations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the active shear area provides a more rational basis for the design of bolted connections failing in block shear than the existing design equations based on the gross and the net shear areas.
the shear failure planes are not necessarily the gross shear planes.
the block shear equations in the design codes should be revised to account for the location of the actual failure planes.
